answer_1.quote: Argument Summarization (ArgSum), a subfield of Argument Mining that focuses on distilling the essence of multiple arguments into concise representations ... We integrate LLMs into existing ArgSum systems, showing substantial performance gains.
answer_1.outputs: argument summaries (key points) generated from a set of arguments

answer_2.quote: We apply the Soft-Score, explained in §3.5, with the following automatic metrics as similarity function f: (1) ROUGE1, (2) BERTScore F1, (3) Mover-Score, (4) BARTScore, (5) BLEURT and (6) MENLI.

answer_3.quote: We introduce two one-shot prompting strategies for assessing ArgSum systems... The LLM-based metric for coverage achieves a maximum correlation of 0.767... The LLM-based metric for redundancy reaches also high correlations...

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation of 126 generated argument summaries... Four experienced annotators ... assess the dimensions of coverage and redundancy... To assess coverage, they are asked to count the number of references that are covered... We then ask the annotators to count the number of unique main statements... We report an average correlation of 0.697 for coverage and 0.722 for redundancy...
answer_4.guideline: Annotators read reference and generated summaries, count covered references for coverage, and count unique main statements for redundancy (uniqueness).
